settings.vietnameseSubtitle: Lễ gia tiên và tiệc cưới
settings.celebration: A Vietnamese–American wedding with a traditional tea ceremony (lễ gia tiên) and a reception.

phases.title: Now – January 2027
phases.summary: Get a rough headcount, choose the Saturday, and book the venue and caterer.

phases.title: Early 2027
phases.summary: Book the planner, local photo and video, officiant, DJ, and confirm Tuấn as MC.

phases.title: Spring – summer 2027
phases.summary: Taste the menu, then book hair and makeup and the flowers.

phases.title: September 2027 · Vietnam
phases.summary: Fittings, the pre-wedding shoot, and printed invitations during the trip.

phases.title: October – November 2027
phases.summary: Alterations at home, cake, and transportation.

phases.title: January – early March 2028
phases.summary: Mail invitations in mid-January, then ceremony details, family roles, and the final headcount.

tasks.title: Get a rough guest count
tasks.notes: Agree on a rough headcount before venue and catering contracts. A precise number comes later, with RSVPs. When you trust a figure, set settings.guestCount.

tasks.title: Choose the wedding date
tasks.notes: Ideal Saturday: March 18, 2028. Alternatives: February 5 or February 19, 2028. Saturday, March 4 is not in the running. Tết Nguyên Đán is January 26, 2028, so each of these dates falls after the holiday. The countdown uses the ideal date until you decide. When you decide, set settings.selectedDate to that Saturday.

tasks.title: Book a reception venue
tasks.notes: Look near Orange and Beaumont, Texas. The venue needs to allow a Vietnamese caterer, or say so if catering is in-house only. Do not assume bring-your-own alcohol: many halls do not allow it, and some allow it only with a licensed bartender. The tea ceremony is at home, so the hall is for the reception.

tasks.title: Host the tea ceremony at home
tasks.notes: Lễ gia tiên will be at one of the couple's homes, not at the reception venue. There is no venue rental. Plan the backdrop, the ancestor altar, flowers, extra chairs and tables for family, the tea set, and the mâm quả trays. The photographer covers the home, and cars are needed between the home and the reception.

tasks.title: Book a Vietnamese caterer
tasks.notes: Book a local Vietnamese caterer for a multi-course menu. Confirm they can work at the reception venue, and plan a tasting once the contract is in place.

tasks.title: Find a planner or day-of coordinator
tasks.notes: No planner is hired yet. Look for someone who has run Vietnamese or Vietnamese–American weddings, including a tea ceremony and a reception.

tasks.title: Book a day-of photographer and videographer
tasks.notes: Coverage starts at the home tea ceremony and continues through the reception. The September 2027 pre-wedding shoot in Vietnam is a separate booking.

tasks.title: Book an officiant
tasks.notes: Book an officiant if you want Western vows along with the tea ceremony. If the tea ceremony is the only rite, mark this done and leave the vendor blank.

tasks.title: Confirm Tuấn as MC
tasks.notes: Confirm that Tuấn can MC. Talk through a bilingual flow so both families can follow the tea ceremony and the reception.

tasks.title: Book a DJ or band
tasks.notes: Book a DJ or band comfortable with Vietnamese and American music, and with handoffs if Tuấn is hosting.

Look for a student or amateur saxophonist for the ceremony entrance and cocktail hour. A short set can complement the DJ or let you book fewer DJ hours. Budget about $200–$500 for an hour, as an estimate, plus travel to Orange or Beaumont.
tasks.title: Music: student sax player (e.g. cocktail hour / ceremony entrance)
Schedule a catering tasting
tasks.notes: Taste the multi-course menu after the caterer is booked. Note dishes to keep, drop, or resize once the guest count is clearer.

tasks.title: Book hair and makeup
tasks.notes: Two looks: áo dài for the tea ceremony, then the reception gown. Ask how long the changeover takes and who is included.

tasks.title: Book florist and decor
tasks.notes: The tea ceremony is at a family home, so include that backdrop, the ancestor altar, and flowers there, plus reception flowers and anything the families will wear or carry.
The reception venue may include tables and chairs. Still price linens, china, and the chairs and tables for family at the home tea ceremony, for 175–250 reception guests.
tasks.title: Book tables, chairs, linens, and china

tasks.notes: Do not assume the reception allows bring-your-own alcohol. Price both a BYO bar with a licensed bartender, where the venue allows it, and a venue bar package. Confirm the rule and the insurance in writing.
tasks.title: Book bartenders and plan the bar

tasks.notes: Decide on 5 or 7 mâm quả trays for the home tea ceremony. Each side needs that many carriers or receivers, traditionally unmarried young relatives or friends. With 4 groomsmen and 4 bridesmaids, 5 trays means one extra person per side and 7 trays means three. Get their measurements before the Vietnam trip so their áo dài can be made or rented.
tasks.title: Choose tray carriers for lễ gia tiên
Dress, áo dài, and suit fittings in Vietnam
tasks.notes: On the September 2027 Vietnam trip, shop and fit the wedding dress, áo dài, and suit. Note what must be finished before the flight home and what can wait for alterations.

tasks.title: Pre-wedding photo shoot in Vietnam
tasks.notes: Schedule the pre-wedding photo shoot during the September 2027 trip. Line it up with fittings so the outfits are ready.

tasks.title: Print bilingual invitations in Vietnam
tasks.notes: Design invitations in English and Vietnamese and print them in Vietnam during the September 2027 trip, in time to mail in mid-January.

tasks.title: Final alterations at home
tasks.notes: After the Vietnam fittings, book final alterations at home for the dress, áo dài, and suit.

tasks.title: Order the cake
tasks.notes: Choose flavor and a size that matches the guest count. Confirm delivery to the reception venue.

tasks.title: Arrange transportation
tasks.notes: The tea ceremony and the reception are in different places. Arrange rides for the couple and for elders between the home and the reception.
Hold a courtesy block near the reception for out-of-town family, in time for a March 18, 2028 wedding. Ask for no-penalty attrition. Guest rooms are paid by the guests.
tasks.title: Set up a hotel room block
Mail the invitations
tasks.notes: Mail invitations in mid-January 2028, about nine weeks before the ideal date of March 18. January 16 is the due date.

The trip is the weekend of January 15, 2028, early to mid January and before Tết on January 26. Options run from a Big Thicket day hike to a 3-day Ouachita backpacking trip. Book any cabins or permits in fall 2027. The group pays its own way; this is not part of the wedding total.
tasks.title: Plan the bachelor hiking trip

tasks.notes: A separate weekend from the hiking trip, on January 8, 2028, still before Tết on January 26. New Orleans is the easy drive. Book lodging in fall 2027. The group pays its own way; this is not part of the wedding total.
tasks.title: Plan the bachelorette weekend

tasks.notes: Texas licenses are valid for 90 days, with a 72-hour wait after issue unless a Twogether in Texas course certificate waives the wait and cuts the fee. March 2 keeps the same lead time before March 18 that January 20 had before a February 5 date.
tasks.title: Get the marriage license
Confirm family elder spokespeople
tasks.notes: Decide who will speak for each family during the tea ceremony.

tasks.title: Decide on a lion dance
tasks.notes: Optional. If you want a lion dance, book the troupe and confirm the venue allows it. If you skip it, clear the vendor fields and mark the task done.

tasks.title: Prepare the mâm quả
tasks.notes: Plan the mâm quả trays for the home tea ceremony: 5 or 7 is traditional, what goes in them, and who carries them. The wedding party is 4 and 4, so 5 trays needs one extra person per side and 7 trays needs three.

tasks.title: Choose the tea set
tasks.notes: Choose the tea set used to serve elders at lễ gia tiên.

tasks.title: Gather ceremony jewelry
tasks.notes: Gather jewelry for the áo dài looks, including anything borrowed from family.

tasks.title: Collect RSVPs and finalize the guest count
tasks.notes: Track replies and set settings.guestCount when the number is firm. Share that count with the venue and the caterer.

weddingParty.summary: Plan on 4 bridesmaids and 4 groomsmen. For lễ gia tiên, the number of mâm quả trays is odd (5 or 7 is common), and each tray has a carrier on the groom's side and a matching receiver on the bride's side, traditionally unmarried young relatives or friends. With 5 trays, each side needs 5 people, so the 4 + 4 party plus one cousin per side covers it. With 7 trays, add 3 per side. Carriers usually wear matching áo dài and receive lì xì.

sources.label: Nicole Bridal: trays are 3, 5, 7, 9 or 11, carried by unmarried young people
USC Folklore Archives: the same number of women receive the baskets

budgetEstimate.summary: Planning ranges for a reception near Orange and Beaumont, with the tea ceremony at home. Wedding-day lines include a 10–15% allowance for tax, tips, and fees. Bachelor and bachelorette costs are shown apart and are not in the wedding total. Figures are estimates unless marked Listed.

lines.basis: Flat rental for the reception only. The tea ceremony is at a family home, so that place costs nothing. The low end is the Brown Estate's published $3,000 reception fee. The high end leaves room for a larger hall, extra hours, and security.

lines.basis: The tea ceremony is at one of the couple's homes. There is no venue rental. Decor, rentals, flowers, and the photographer are on their own lines.

Per guest, food plus staff, service, and travel if the kitchen is in Houston. A Houston Vietnamese restaurant prices a 10-person family dinner around $30–$37 a head before off-site staffing. The Knot's national wedding-dinner average sits higher, so the high end is $85. The $50k plan uses a family-style banquet near the low end. Estimate.

The tea ceremony is planned at a family home, so the altar there is not under this rule. Music ends by 11 pm. vendorOptions.pricing: 3-day backpacking weekend. Gas, gear, food, maybe a cabin the night before.
vendorOptions.fit: Real hills: a 26.8-mile loop over ridges, past a big waterfall and up to the Eagle Rock vista. The best fit if the groom wants a challenge.
vendorOptions.caveat: Strenuous, with many cold river crossings in winter. Everyone needs to be fit and have done some backpacking.

vendorOptions.name: New Orleans weekend
vendorOptions.pricing: Commonly $400–$1,000 a person for a drive-to weekend.
vendorOptions.fit: The easy drive-to choice from Orange, about four hours away, with food tours, swamp tours and the French Quarter.
vendorOptions.caveat: Carnival season starts January 6 and Mardi Gras is February 29, 2028. Parade weekends push hotel prices up, so check the parade calendar.
